briefings.plainEnglish:
Stirling, Edition 64

The Japanese Yen gained significantly against the US Dollar today, with USD/JPY falling by 2.25%. This was the most unusual move on the board, registering 3.9 standard deviations against its trailing month.

Meanwhile, the UK 10-year Gilt saw its yield climb by 7.0 basis points, a move of 1.8 standard deviations. Gold also rose, increasing by 3.53%, consistent with reports that Nvidia has struck a $12.9 billion deal to acquire the AI platform Hugging Face.

Other notable movements included the UK 20-year Gilt, which saw its yield rise by 6.28 basis points, and the UK 5-year Gilt, up 6.81 basis points. Bitcoin also climbed, increasing by 5.28%.

What to watch tomorrow:
1. The ongoing situation regarding gas prices, following warnings that a spike could pressure energy bills.
2. Any further developments related to the EU and Nato's vow to increase pressure on Russia.
3. The continuing discussion around AI data centres, particularly their booming growth and associated costs.
